(*) There is a fundamental diﬀ erence between the Hindi and English versions of the above question. In the Hindi format the question has asked about the oﬃ cial language in context of Constitution of India whereas in the English format the question focuses on the Parliament's authority of amending the oﬃ cial language of India. Hence, the nuances so present, create a contradictory nature among the intellects to resort to a conclusion. D–359 General Studies Indian Polity and Governance *Part XVII of the constitution deals with the oﬃ cial language in Article 343 to 351. Its provisions are divided into four heads- a. Language of the Union b. Regional Languages c. Language of the Judiciary d. Texts of Laws and special directives Thus it is quite evident from above context that the term 'The Oﬃ cial Language of India' is nonewhere mentioned in the Indian constitution. If we ignore the above mentioned 'mistake' or 'ambiguity' for the quiz, then it seems that the question relates to "the oﬃ cial language of the Union". As mentioned in the ﬁ rst paragraph of this interpretation, due to the diﬀ erence between the Hindi and English forms of the question, the answer will also be diﬀ erent. According to Hindi form, option (b) is correct. Amendment to Article 343, 344, 346 and 348 (1) (b) is possible only by the Parliament according to the overwhelming process mentioned in Article 368 (2), otherwise not. The amendment in above mentioned Articles i.e. 343, 344, 346 & 348 (1) does not require ratiﬁ cation of the state legislatures. On the other hand, if the English form of the question is accepted, then option (a) will be the correct answer. According to article 343 (3) of constitution, Parliament is authorised for creating an exception to Article 343 (1). As per Article 100 (1), such a law will be made by Parliament with its simple majority. The Parliament has enacted the Oﬃ cial Language Act, 1963, using its power. According to Section 3 of this Act, in addition to Hindi, English will also be used as the oﬃ cial language of the Union, from January 26, 1965. For some of the Union Government's purposes, English is mandatory. Clearly, any amendment in the said act can be made by Parliament with its simple majority and accordingly, the oﬃ cial language of the Union can be amended according to the constitution. The word 'Provision' used in the English form of the question and the word 'Under the constitution' are being clariﬁ ed in the article 343 (3) of the constitution. Thus to elucidate there are two distinct answers to the same question. 15. Panchayati Raj and Community Development *Panchayati Raj is the system of democratic decentralisation. Its objective is to bring the development to grass root level. *There are provisions related to Panchayati Raj in part-IX from Article 243 to Act 243 (O) in the Indian-constitution. *16 New Articles in part-IX and 11th schedule was added in Indian constitution by the 73rd constitutional Amendment Act 1992. Total 29 subjects are mentioned in 11th schedule providing power to panchayats to make laws. *Panchayati Raj is a subject of state list. *The state legislature determines provisions related to the structure of panchayats. *The state legislature take decisions with respect to all matters relating to elections to the Panchayat. *It is conducted after every 5 year. *There is a provision to form Finance commission to review ﬁ nancial condition of panchayats. *'Gram Sabha, is formed by the people registered in electoral rolls of a village. *Article 40 of Indian constitution directs the state for organisation of village panchayats. *Balwant Rai Mehta committee recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system at-Village level, Block level and District level. *Balwant Rai Mehta is called Architect of Panchayati Raj system. *The inauguration of Panchayati Raj system was done by Pt. Jawahar lal Nehru on 2nd October 1959 at Nagaur (Rajasthan). *Panchayati Raj institutions got constitutional status by 73rd constitutional Amendment Act. *Firstly Laxmi Mal Singhvi committee in 1986 and then P.K. Thungan committee in 1988 recommended panchayati Raj Institutions to be given constitutional status. *Earlier, Ashok Mehta committee, in 1977 proposed that some provisions of Panchayati Raj are capable to be kept in Indian constitution, so Government of India should think over it. *Due to collapse of the Janta Government no action could be taken on the recommendations of the Ashok Mehta Committee at the central Level. *So only the recommendations of Laxmi Mal Singhvi and P.K. Thungan committee are clearly accepted. *According to Article 243-D(3), women are given 1/3rd reservation at all levels of Panchayats. *The minimum age to become a member of Panchayat is 21 years. *74th constitutional amendment Act 1992 gives constitutional status to the urban local self-government. *By this Amendment Act a new part [part IX (A)] and 12th schedule was added into the constitution. *There are 8 types of local self-government which includes Municipal corporation, Municipality, Notiﬁ ed Area Committee, D–361 General Studies Indian Polity and Governance Town Area Committee, Cantonment Board, Township, Port trust and Special Purpose Agencies. *74th Amendment Act provides three types of municipalities. *This includes Municipal corporation, Municipal council and a Nagar Panchayat. *All the members of the municipality were elected by the people of that area directly. *The term of municipality is 5 years but it can be terminated earlier also. *State election commission has the right to direct, control and manage the election for the municipalities. *A Finance commission is constituted under article 243 (I) to review ﬁ nancial condition of municipalities. *A District Planning committee is constituted under Article 243 ZD (1) at District level to consolidate the plans prepared by the municipalities in the district and to draft a development plan for the district as a whole. *According to Article 243ZE, in every metropolitan area, a metropolitan planning committee is to be constituted, to prepare a draft development plan for the metropolitan area as a whole. *In India the ﬁ rst municipal corporation was established in Madras in the year 1688. *Lord Ripon is known as the father of local self-government in India. 1. Nominated members participate in the meeting and can vote. Code : (a) i iv vi (b) iii v vi (c) ii iii vi (d) iv v vi (e) None of these Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2015 Ans. (c) Gram Panchayats are the smallest unit of local self- governance, at village level. According to Chhattisgarh Panchayati Raj Act, (1993), each Gram Panchayat area is divided into not less than 10 and not more than 20 wards and each ward elects one Panch. The Gram Panchayat consists of the elected Panchs plus a Sarpanch who is the head of the Gram Panchayat. Thus all member are elected not nominated. So option (ii), (iii) and (vi) are wrong. 4. Sarpanch can be dismissed if Quorum is not present in ﬁ ve subsequent meetings of Gram Sabha. Choose the incorrect statements using the code given below. Code: A B C (a) i ii v (b) iii vi viii (c) iv vii viii (d) v vi vii (e) vi vii viii Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2015 Ans. (d) According to Chhattisgarh Panchayati Raj Act 1993 as amended in 2004, a Gram Sabha must meet once every three months in a year. The presence of 1/10th of the total number of members of Gram Sabha of whom 1/3rd must be women, constitutes the quorum for a Gram Sabha meeting.
